input.heading: How information moves
input.lead: Atkinson and Shiffrin proposed separate stores linked by control processes.
points: Attention selects sensory information for STM.
Maintenance rehearsal repeats information in STM.
Retrieval brings stored information from LTM to STM.

figure.shows: The multi-store model, including the rehearsal loop and transfer to long-term memory
figure.alt: Attention links the sensory register to STM; rehearsal loops in STM and supports transfer to LTM; retrieval returns information to STM.

input.heading: Glanzer and Cunitz: serial position
input.lead: Word-list recall was compared immediately and after a filled delay that prevented rehearsal.

points.label: Primacy
points.text: Early words: more rehearsal and LTM storage.

points.label: Recency
points.text: Final words: available in STM at immediate recall.

figure.shows: Schematic serial position curves: early-word recall remains relatively high after a filled delay, but the final-word advantage is reduced
figure.alt: Both curves show good early-word recall. Immediate recall also shows good final-word recall, while delayed recall loses much of that final-word advantage.

slide.heading: How information moves
slide.lead: Atkinson and Shiffrin proposed three separate memory stores linked by control processes.
points: Attention selects information from the sensory register and transfers it to short-term memory (STM).
Maintenance rehearsal repeats information in STM. Rehearsal may support transfer from STM to long-term memory (LTM).
Retrieval brings information from LTM back into STM.
